To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) The presence of HCO3 (and CO2), which are the products of CO2 hydration, are essential for the Ca2+‐dependent Iscc and Ca(2+)i oscillations, which occur after stimulation with the choline receptor agonist MCh in human cultured sweat duct epithelial cells (CSDC).
HCO3‐ and CO2 are important factors for the function of human sweat gland duct cells.
the cholinergic response of CSDCs is critically dependent on the presence of extracellualr HCO3‐ in the bathing solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of extracellular H+ (HCO3‐) on the Iscc and Ca(2+)i in CSDC.
the influence of extracellular bicarbonated (CO2/HCO3‐) on the short‐current and intracellular free Calcium in human sweat duct cell.

the influence of extracellular H+ (and CO2), which are present in the sweat duct lumen, on the transepithelial short circuit current and on the intracellular free calcium concentration in human cultured sweat duct epithelium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HCO3‐/CO2‐dependent Ca2+ entry is an important mechanism in CSDCs.
the presence of HCO3− (and CO2), in the bathing solution, is essential for the Ca(2+)-mediated Iscc response in CSDCs.
the HCO3‐ effect is confined to the serosa and that it is involved in the generation of Iscc and Ca(2+)i oscillations in CSDCs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cholinergic stimulation of the CSDCs induces a biphasic response.
CSDC are a good model to study the role of HCO3− in the regulation of Ca2+ and fluid secretion in the skin.
HCO3‐ is an important regulator of the Ca(2+) signalling and transepithelial Iscc in CDSs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HCO3‐‐induced increase in Iscc and Ca(2+) oscillations is not mediated by an increase in Ca(2+) influx but rather by a modulation of Ca(2+) release from intracellular stores.
the HCO3‐‐dependent Iscc in sweat gland duct cells is not a passive process.

the presence of HCO3 in the bathing solutions is a prerequisite for the generation of the sustained Iscc and the Ca2+i oscillation in CSDCs, which may be of relevance for the function of human sweat glands in vivo.
